clue.text: Lofty monarch portrayed in drawing

indicators.note: the monarch is placed inside the word for drawing, as if portrayed within it

parts.note: drawing a trailer or barge is towing it
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword monarch

explanation.surface: A tall king is shown in a sketch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawing' suggests a picture, but here it means hauling along; 'portrayed' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Lofty and towering both describe something rising very high.

clue.text: Final part in current agenda

indicators.note: in shows the letters sit inside the words current agenda

explanation.surface: The last item is on the agenda now in force.
explanation.definitionFit: A tag end is the last remaining bit or tail of something.

clue.text: Spa treatment with unusual care? True

indicators.note: unusual signals the letters of care and true are put in an odd order

explanation.surface: A spa offers therapy with surprising attentiveness, it is claimed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusual' is the anagram signal for the eight letters of 'care' and 'True'; the question mark merely dresses the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Hydropathy, treating ailments by bathing in or drinking spring water, is a spa therapy.

clue.text: Flashy servicemen flounder, perhaps

parts.note: the RAF, Royal Air Force, are servicemen
a flounder is one example of a fish

explanation.surface: Air force men in loud clothes splash about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flounder' reads as a verb of struggling, but is the flatfish.
explanation.definitionFit: Raffish means showily disreputable, flashy in a rakish way.

clue.text: Confirmation ultimately at church, of course

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word confirmation

explanation.surface: A confirmation service finally happens at church, naturally.
explanation.definitionFit: Natch is slang shortened from naturally, meaning obviously.

clue.text: Roman general, one featured in old pictures brought back

indicators.note: brought back tells us to read the assembled letters in reverse order
featured in means the word for one appears inside the other pieces

parts.note: pics is short for pictures
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A Roman general appears once more in old photographs that have been revived.
explanation.walkthrough: I goes into O + PICS to make OIPICS, which 'brought back' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: Scipio Africanus was the commander who beat Hannibal for Rome.

clue.text: Crash into vehicle with a shout of surprise

indicators.note: into places the crash word inside the vehicle word

parts.note: a cab is a vehicle
to crash into something is to ram it

explanation.surface: Someone drives into another car and cries out in shock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crash into' reads as one phrase, but 'into' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A Spanish exclamation of astonishment, much used in comics and westerns.

clue.text: Time off work father put before employment

indicators.note: put before places the father word ahead of the employment word

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
employment of a tool is its use

explanation.surface: Dad took leave from his job before landing new work.
explanation.definitionFit: A pause is a short break or rest from activity.

clue.text: Dear antique

explanation.surface: Something precious is very old.
explanation.definitionFit: An affectionate form of address between friends, and literally an aged object.

clue.text: Dog as circus performer with unknown actor

parts.note: a seal balancing a ball is a traditional circus act
Y is one of the algebraic unknowns
a ham is an overacting actor

explanation.surface: A dog works in a circus act alongside a mediocre thespian.
explanation.walkthrough: A Sealyham is a small Welsh terrier.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sealyham terrier is a breed named after a house in Pembrokeshire.

clue.text: Ref's words to offending player begin to take effect

explanation.surface: A referee orders a culprit off the pitch as things start to happen.
explanation.definitionFit: A referee might literally tell a fallen player to rise from the turf; the idiom means a project starts successfully.

clue.text: Being stupid hinders criminal

indicators.note: criminal as an adjective suggests the letters are treated wrongly and rearranged

explanation.surface: Foolishness gets in the way of a crook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' looks like the noun subject; it signals rearranging HINDERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting like a socially awkward, obsessive swot can be described as geeky; the definition takes it as daft behaviour.

clue.text: A walk in part of London?

definitions.text: A walk in part of London?

parts.words: A walk in part of London?
parts.note: a popular 1930s song-and-dance number is named after a walk in a south London borough

explanation.surface: Someone takes a stroll through a district of the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lambeth Walk is a famous Cockney dance from the 1937 musical Me and My Girl; Lambeth is a borough of south London.
explanation.definitionFit: The borough gave its name to a well-known dance called a walk.

clue.text: Bird starts to nest under straw roof

indicators.note: starts to tells us to take the opening letters of the following words

parts.note: a roof of straw or reeds is a thatch

explanation.surface: A bird begins nesting under a cottage's thatched roof.
explanation.definitionFit: The nuthatch is a small climbing woodland songbird.

clue.text: Went to bed, hearing seabird's noise?

indicators.note: hearing signals that what we want sounds like the words that follow

parts.note: a tern is a seabird and din is noise, together tern din

explanation.surface: Someone retired for the night, kept awake by gulls squawking.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn in is an idiom for going to bed.

clue.text: Girl repulsed by a high priest

indicators.note: repulsed means pushed back, so the girl's name is read backwards

parts.note: Nora is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A young woman rejects the advances of a senior cleric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' simply places A beside the reversed NORA.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible, Moses's brother was the first high priest of the Israelites.

clue.text: Wander round the outskirts of rough northern town

indicators.note: round means the wandering word goes around the other letters

parts.note: to wander is to roam

indicators.note: outskirts of means the outer letters of the word rough

explanation.surface: A traveller roams the fringes of a rough town in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round' is the container signal; 'outskirts of' takes the outer letters of 'rough'. Rotherham is in South Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotherham is a South Yorkshire town in the north of England.

clue.text: Supports short branches, say

indicators.note: say indicates a soundalike of the shoots word

parts.note: suckers are short shoots growing from a plant's root or base

explanation.surface: Small boughs hold something up, for example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' could mean 'for example', but it signals a homophone.
explanation.definitionFit: To succour is to help or aid someone in need.

clue.text: In court after exploit, get exhausted

indicators.note: after places the court word following the exploit word

parts.note: to exploit something is to use it
someone up before the judge is in court

explanation.surface: Having taken advantage, someone finds themselves on trial and worn out.
explanation.definitionFit: To consume completely is to make a supply be exhausted.

clue.text: Artist's model briefly hosting us at home

indicators.note: hosting means the model word contains the next piece
briefly means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: to model is to pose
someone in is at home

explanation.surface: A painter's sitter has a brief session with us at the house.
explanation.walkthrough: POSE loses its end to give POS, which holds US; IN follows. The 's in 'Artist's' stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicolas Poussin was a leading French Baroque painter.

clue.text: Think Martinu composed with energy

indicators.note: composed suggests putting the letters together in a new arrangement, fitting for a composer

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Martinu, the Czech composer, writes music with vigour and thought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Composed' fits the composer Martinu but signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: To ponder or mull over is to think deeply.

clue.text: Unpleasant people vandalised Staines

indicators.note: vandalised means the letters of the town name are damaged and rearranged

explanation.surface: Thugs have trashed the town of Staines.
explanation.walkthrough: Staines is a town west of London near Heathrow.
explanation.definitionFit: Nasties are nasty characters, unpleasant folk.

clue.text: Ex-student's in step

parts.note: a grad, or graduate, has finished being a student

explanation.surface: A graduate is in tune with everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In step' reads as a phrase, but 'step' is the definition alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A gradin is one of a tier of seats or steps, as in an amphitheatre.

clue.text: For party, you'll need transport 'ome

parts.note: a car is a means of transport
'ome is home with the H dropped, Cockney-style, so it stands for house dropping its H

explanation.surface: To get to the party you will need a lift back to your house.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in ''ome' shows a dropped H, so it asks for 'ouse, house without its H.
explanation.definitionFit: To carouse is to drink and celebrate noisily, as at a party.

clue.text: Assailant eliminating a cavalryman, say

indicators.note: eliminating means one letter is taken away

parts.note: a raider is an attacker

explanation.surface: An attacker kills a mounted soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: A cavalryman is one example of a horseman.

clue.text: Scientist in bygone era given endless foreign cash?

parts.note: a bygone era is the past

indicators.note: endless means the final letter of the currency word is removed

parts.note: the euro is a currency foreign to Britain

explanation.surface: A scientist from long ago is handed overseas money that never runs out.
explanation.definitionFit: Louis Pasteur was the French chemist behind pasteurisation and vaccines.

clue.text: Right-hand man acquires German communication device

parts.note: a PA, personal assistant, is a boss's right-hand man

explanation.surface: An assistant gets hold of a German gadget for messaging.
explanation.definitionFit: A bleeper receives short messages, a device for being contacted.

clue.text: Ordinary, so not recognized?

explanation.surface: Something plain goes unnoticed for that reason.
explanation.definitionFit: It means unremarkable, and read literally it means not told apart or picked out.

clue.text: Team player having to prepare racket

explanation.surface: A sportsman joins a side and gets his tennis gear ready.
explanation.walkthrough: A team's players are ranked first string, second string and so on; to string a racket is to fit its strings.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of a squad ranked by strength is a string; fitting the gut to a racket is stringing it.

clue.text: First-class student?

parts.note: not a top scholar but one in the first-year intake of a college

explanation.surface: A brilliant pupil earns top marks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First-class' suggests excellence; it means belonging to the first year's class.
explanation.definitionFit: An American term for a first-year undergraduate.
